input_signals.name: AcquiredIntangibleAccrualInflation
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(intan, at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: When a firm expands its capitalized intangible base (acquisitions, capitalized development, purchase-price allocation), the acquired operations arrive with receivables and inventory that are recognized before cash conversion is verified; working-capital accruals booked during intangible expansion are therefore far more likely to reverse than the same accruals at a stable-intangible firm.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual leg is kept in its standard asset-scaled form (no deflator surgery, so no small-denominator instability), and the intangible theme enters as a bounded 0-1 conditioning weight on the change in intangible share, which is the purchase-accounting channel rather than the R&D-expense channel used in the accepted signal. The signal is near zero for firms with flat intangible intensity regardless of their accruals, so the bet is explicitly on accruals generated inside intangible expansion rather than on the Sloan effect itself.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ratio( intan, at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualUptrendAgainstRnDDowntrend
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5), 1)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(xrd, sale), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms harvesting accounting earnings from a shrinking innovation base are the clearest case of accrual-driven rather than productive earnings: a multi-year rise in the accrual share of income combined with a multi-year decline in R&D intensity signals substitution of accounting income for real intangible investment, and both components reverse.
input_signals.reasoning: The near-constant TS_COUNT leg is dropped entirely, so nothing collapses to plain R&D intensity; instead both themes enter as five-year directional states, with the signed accrual trend as the bet and the R&D-intensity downtrend rank as the conditioning weight. Firms whose intangible commitment is rising receive near-zero weight even with rising accruals, which is the divergence concept the earlier version only claimed.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( trend( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 5 ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( xrd, sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: SlowAmortizationIntangibleOverhang
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(intan, at)), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dp, at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The non-cash charge dp is the accrual through which capitalized intangibles are expensed; an intangible-heavy balance sheet carried with unusually light depreciation and amortization means the intangible stock is being written off too slowly, inflating current earnings and storing up impairment risk.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the deflator-swap logic and the ceq denominator entirely — no small or negative scaler appears, since both legs are scaled by total assets and one leg is a bounded rank. The economic content is a true cross-theme conjunction: low amortization intensity is only diagnostic when there is a large capitalized intangible stock to amortize, so tangible firms with low dp/at receive near-zero signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( intan, at ) ), neg( zscore( winsor( ratio( dp, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: GrossMarginGatedAccrualOverhang
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross margin is a full-sample proxy for knowledge/brand capital that is expensed rather than capitalized: high-margin firms earn rents from intangibles that never appear on the balance sheet, and their earnings are correspondingly harder to audit, so accrual-driven income reverses more strongly there than at low-margin, tangible processing firms.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the xrd gate (coverage 0.047) with an intangible-rent proxy available for essentially every firm, so the same conditional mechanism as the accepted gen-0 winner can be tested with roughly ten times the observations. The accrual leg is industry-z-scored so the long-short spread is not simply a bet on high-margin industries, which is the composition problem that killed the SlowAmortization alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: IntangibleAdjustedGrossProfitCleanAccruals
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Productive intangible investment shows up as gross profit generated per dollar of intangible-augmented capital; the market rewards this only when the profit is cash-backed, because gross profitability at chronically accrual-heavy firms is itself an artifact of revenue recognition rather than of output.
input_signals.reasoning: Every prior bet leg has been an input measure (how much intangible capital the firm holds); this is the first output measure — the return on that capital — which directly implements the task's mandate to separate productive intangible investment from accounting-driven earnings. Capitalizing R&D into the denominator makes the profitability metric comparable across expensing regimes, so the interaction is intrinsic rather than a bolted-on gate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PreRnDEconomicEarningsCleanAccruals
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 3), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Reported income understates the economic profitability of research-intensive firms because R&D is a discretionary investment charged against current earnings; profitability measured before the intangible investment charge is the true productive-capacity measure, and it is credible only where the accrual record shows the income converts to cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The bet leg changes from an intangible *stock* to an expensing-corrected *earnings* concept, so this asks a different economic question than the archived winner — whether mispricing comes from unbooked capital or from understated current profitability — and the two can be told apart by their alphas. Smoothing profitability over three years matches the gate's horizon and avoids one-year expense timing artifacts.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ma( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: TripleGateIntangibleQuality
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 3)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Separating productive intangible investment from accounting-driven earnings requires three simultaneous conditions: the firm must actually hold deep expensed intangible capital, that capital must generate economic (pre-R&D) profits, and those profits must convert to cash. Failing any one condition disqualifies the firm.
input_signals.reasoning: The two-way conjunction already improved on the multiplicative form, so the open question is whether adding the pre-R&D economic-earnings channel — which carried the archive's best FMB slope of 4.05 — sharpens the long leg further or merely thins it. Nested MINs keep every input on a common bounded scale, and the outcome tells us whether the mechanism is about capital, about returns on that capital, or about both.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), min( rank( ma( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WithinIndustryConjunctiveIntangibleQuality
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Both intangible depth and earnings quality are only interpretable against industry norms — a 3%-of-assets R&D stock is deep for a manufacturer and trivial for a biotech, and accrual conventions differ by business model — so the mispriced firms are those that are unusual on both dimensions relative to their peers.
input_signals.reasoning: The industry question remains unresolved because the one industry-demeaned long-side attempt changed two levers at once and collapsed, while the industry-relative gate on the short side worked well; running it inside the now-best conjunctive structure gives a clean answer. If alpha survives, the family's returns are genuine within-industry mispricing rather than an unpriced sector tilt, which materially strengthens the economic interpretation for the final generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: UnprofitableAccrualSupportedIntangibleFirms
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The genuinely overpriced corner is not merely intangible-heavy plus accrual-supported, but intangible-heavy, accrual-supported *and* economically unprofitable even before the R&D charge — a firm burning resources on an intangible story while reporting income it cannot collect.
input_signals.reasoning: The two-way "both-bad" conjunction failed (t = -1.46, wrong-signed FMB) because intangible-heavy accrual users include many profitable firms whose accruals are working-capital growth, not manipulation; adding the pre-R&D profitability screen removes them and isolates the value-destroying subset. This repairs the family's weak short side using the same profitability dimension that produced the strongest cross-sectional slopes on the long side.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ), min( rank( ratio( add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RentMarginIntangibleQualityConjunction
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Productive intangible investment must eventually manifest as pricing power: a deep R&D stock that earns no gross margin is a cost centre, not an asset. Requiring high margins, deep intangible capital, and cash-backed earnings simultaneously identifies firms whose expensed investment has actually created an economic moat.
input_signals.reasoning: The third gate in the current leader is pre-R&D ROA, which shares the ib term with the accrual gate and is therefore mechanically correlated with it; gross margin is an independent, revenue-side manifestation of intangible rents, so this tests whether the triple-gate improvement comes from profitability information generally or specifically from the bottom-line channel. Gross margin failed earlier only as a multiplicative weight on one-year accruals, a construction the archive has since shown to be the weakest available form.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ) ), min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: TwoCornerIntangibleAccountingSpread
input_signals.expression: SUB(MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 3))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The two economically identified corners of this problem are distinct populations, not opposite ends of one variable: productive intangible investors (deep expensed capital, chronically cash-backed earnings) and accounting-driven intangible stories (intangible-heavy, accrual-supported, unprofitable before research). A signal that scores membership in the first corner net of membership in the second targets exactly the firms the mechanism says should diverge.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's long-side and short-side constructs have always been separate signals whose extreme deciles are populated by whichever firms happen to be at the tail of a single score; here both corners are defined by explicit conjunctions and differenced, so the long and short legs are each economically identified rather than residually determined. This is a consolidation with new structure rather than the mechanical lever-crossing the critic rejected, and it directly targets alpha magnitude by ensuring neither leg is diluted by firms that merely fail the opposite criterion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) ) ), min( rank( ratio( add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ), min( rank( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 3 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PreResearchCashGenerationIntangibleCapital
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Because research spending is a cash operating outflow, reported operating cash flow understates the cash-generating power of research-intensive firms exactly as reported earnings understate their profitability; pre-research operating cash flow is the correct measure of the franchise's capacity to fund its own intangible investment, and deep intangible capital is credible only where that capacity exists.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the critic's accounting error by *adding* R&D back to oancf rather than subtracting it again, making the gate the cash-flow analogue of the pre-R&D earnings measure that produced the archive's strongest FMB slope (4.05). It is distinct from cash-based operating profitability, which starts from gross profit and deducts working-capital accruals, and it asks a different question from the accrual gate: not whether earnings convert to cash, but whether the business generates cash before it chooses how much to invest in intangibles.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: NoAggressiveAccrualEpisodeIntangibleCapital
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Earnings management is episodic rather than average: a firm that has never had a single aggressive accrual year over a full investment cycle has a credibly conservative reporting culture, whereas an averaged record can hide one large manipulation offset by several quiet years. Intangible capital is worth capitalizing only at firms whose worst accounting year was still clean.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a lookback-window tweak but a change of statistic — an extremum criterion instead of a central-tendency one — which separates firms with persistent conservatism from firms whose mean is clean only because manipulations cancel. Given that lengthening the averaging window already improved results, the interesting economic question is whether the improvement came from more data or from suppressing episodic aggressiveness, and only the worst-case statistic can answer it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ts_max( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashAndAccrualDoubleGatedIntangibleCapital
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash generation and accrual conservatism are economically distinct certifications of an intangible program — the first says the franchise produces cash, the second says reported income is not manufactured — and a firm satisfying both is the least likely to be an accounting artifact.
input_signals.reasoning: The two gates delivered similar alphas separately (+6.9% and +6.2%) but they are not mechanically equivalent: a firm can generate strong pre-research cash flow while still running aggressive accruals, and vice versa. Whether requiring both raises the alpha or merely thins the long leg is the single most useful thing to learn before the final specification, because it determines whether the remaining generations should refine one gate or keep both.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), min( rank( winsor( ratio( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: BuildVersusBuyAccrualSpread
input_signals.expression: SUB(MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at), 1)))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms build intangible capital in two ways and the accounting consequences are opposite: internally generated research is expensed and invisible, while acquired intangibles are capitalized at negotiated prices and arrive with the working-capital positions of the target. The mispricing is concentrated where the build route is paired with conservative working-capital accruals and where the buy route is paired with accrual expansion.
input_signals.reasoning: The two corners now differ in the *intangible* dimension (internally generated versus purchased) as well as in accrual orientation, so the spread is an economic contrast between modes of intangible creation rather than a mirrored gate swap. The accrual term is the noncash, debt-excluded balance-sheet construction, which contains neither ib nor oancf, eliminating the shared-term mechanics the critic identified in the previous short corner.
input_signals.author: proposer

input_signals.name: CashReturnOnIntangibleAugmentedCapital
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Expensing distorts both sides of a profitability ratio for research-intensive firms: cash flow is understated because research was paid in cash, and the capital base is understated because the resulting asset was never booked. Correcting both gives a cash return on true invested capital that is comparable across expensing regimes, and deep intangible capital is only valuable where that return is high.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a smoothing tweak of the existing gate but a change of the measured quantity — from cash generation per accounting dollar of assets to cash return on intangible-augmented capital — which removes the mechanical advantage asset-light research firms enjoy in the current denominator. If it beats the asset-scaled version, the mechanism is about genuine capital productivity; if it does not, the premium attaches to asset-light business models, and that distinction matters for the final specification.

input_signals.name: IntangibleCapitalProductivityCleanBalanceSheet
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Productive intangible investment is identified by gross output per dollar of intangible-augmented capital, and it is credible only when that output is not accompanied by an expanding stock of uncollected claims; the two together separate firms whose research produces sellable product from firms whose revenue is a receivable.
input_signals.reasoning: This construct deliberately avoids ib and oancf entirely, using only gross profit, the intangible-augmented capital base, and the noncash balance-sheet accrual, so it provides an independent accounting basis for the family's central claim rather than another combination of the same two line items. If it performs comparably to the cash-flow-gated leaders, the mechanism is robust to the accounting surface used to measure earnings quality, which materially strengthens the economic interpretation.

input_signals.name: LeanWorkingCapitalIntangibleFranchise
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A business model that requires little net operating working capital per dollar of revenue collects quickly and finances itself from customers rather than from investors; combined with deep expensed intangible capital, this identifies franchises whose research output converts directly into cash rather than into inventory and receivables.
input_signals.reasoning: The critic correctly showed that DELTA(wcap) contaminates the intended reading because wcap includes cash and current debt; this uses the noncash, debt-excluded operating working-capital *level* scaled by sales, so a firm converting research into cash is not penalized for holding that cash. Measuring the stock rather than the annual change also captures a structural business-model attribute rather than a one-year accrual, which is a different economic concept from every gate tested so far.

input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(oancf, SUB(ADD(ib, dp), SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))))), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating cash flow is economically defined as earnings plus depreciation less the noncash working-capital accrual, so where the cash-flow statement is unavailable the same quantity can be reconstructed from the balance sheet; the mechanism should hold identically for firms measured either way, because the construct — cash generated before research spending — is the same.

If alpha and the FMB slope survive at higher coverage, the result is substantially more credible and no longer confined to the post-cash-flow-statement sample.

input_signals.name: InternalNetAcquiredDoubleGated
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The mispriced asset is internally generated intangible capital that never entered book value, so purchased goodwill should be netted out of the bet leg; combined with cash generation and accrual conservatism, this identifies firms whose understated book value is a consequence of expensing rather than of acquisition accounting.
input_signals.reasoning: The internal-minus-acquired bet leg beat the plain R&D stock in both functional forms tested (alpha +6.0% multiplicative, +5.4% conjunctive with Sharpe 0.508), and the double gate is the current best gate configuration, but the two have never been paired. This is the natural best-of-each-leg consolidation for the final specification, and its outcome tells us whether goodwill netting adds beyond what the earnings-quality gates already remove.

input_signals.name: StructuralWorkingCapitalCashGatedIntangibles
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 1)))))
